text: The exponential time hypothesis is false! Let 2^{e(K)·K²λ}·poly(λ) be the time to contract tensor networks on K_K with λ bits per edge and arbitrary node tensors. Then e(9K^16) ≤ 0.9·e(K) + O(1/K). Put the nodes on a grid: the two diagonals of each rectangle form a swap. Per bit, SWAP = I − 2·singlet; grouping by the number of singlets gives λ+1 operators with (row rank)·(column rank) ≤ 12^λ. For each choice of operators, merge each row or each column into one node, whichever is cheaper, and regroup these into K balanced classes. Prove it. A deterministic algorithm solves 3-SAT on n variables in time 2 o( n ) , which refutes the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH). The algorithm in fact solves the harder problem #3-SAT, counting the satisfying assignments, in time 2 O( n log log n / √log n ) . The result is purely asymptotic and says nothing about solving formulas in practice. The result was discovered by an internal research Claude model. This folder holds the paper and its Lean 4 formalization, which was written by AI models. Research artifact. Not maintained and not accepting contributions. paper.pdf : A 2 o(n) Time Algorithm for 3-SAT , by Claude (Anthropic). Hexagon link to appear. 1. Read the statement. One commented file, MainResults.lean , states what is proved, on Mathlib's Turing machines: The file contains no proofs and imports nothing but Mathlib. Lean checks the proofs, but no machine checks that this file says what the paper says; the file is kept short so that a reader can check this. Appendix E of the paper prints it and lists how it differs from the printed statements. proof/PaperIndex.lean lists, for each numbered statement of the paper, its Lean counterpart, and says where the Lean form differs. 2. Check the proofs. With elan installed, in this folder ( cd eth ): lake exe cache get lake build lake env lean scripts/PrintAxioms.lean The first command downloads Mathlib already compiled. The build took about 8 minutes on 24 virtual CPUs, and its largest process used about 7 GB of memory. It prints two warnings declaration uses `sorry` , both from Challenge.lean , which states the two theorems without proofs for the fuller check below. The last command should print: 'MainResults.ethIsFalse' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] 'MainResults.mainTheorem' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] Those are Lean's three standard axioms. Lean v4.33.1 and the matching Mathlib, also v4.33.1 , are pinned. The fuller check is the one this repository's CI runs, bash ../.github/scripts/comparator-check.sh (Linux): Comparator also compares the theorems' statements with Challenge.lean and re-checks the proofs with a second, independently written kernel, nanoda .
